items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S7027

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public health law and the
administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to
prohibiting the sale of liquid nicotine to minors

PURPOSE:

This bill would prohibit the sale of liquid nicotine to minors.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends Section 1399-cc of the public health law, as
amended by chapter 131 of the laws of 2011, subdivisions 2, 3, 4 and 7
as amended by chapter 448 of the laws of 2012.

Section two amends Section 17-706 of the administrative code of the
city of New York, as amended by local law number 94 of the city of New
York.

Section three sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

E-cigarettes are currently not allowed to be sold to minors. This ban
became effective January 1, 2013. E-cigarettes are battery powered
devices that allow an individual to inhale nicotine while emitting
only vapor. The nicotine in e-cigarettes is called "electronic
liquids" or "liquid nicotine". Liquid nicotine is a liquid composed of
nicotine but is also laced with other chemicals and substances and is
often flavored. Many liquid nicotine compounds are made on factory
floors or in the back rooms of shops and are not regulated by the
federal government. Currently, liquid nicotine is sold in sealed
cartridges or in a bottle used to refill e-cigarettes or refillable
cartridges.

This bill would ban the sale of liquid nicotine to minors. This
legislation will protect children from the potential dangers of
electronic cigarettes, particularly given that they are unregulated
and have not been proven to be safe for use at any age.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that if
local law number 94 of the city of New York for the year 2013 shall
not have taken effect on or before such date then section two of this
act shall take effect on the same date and in the same manner as local
law number 94 of the city of New York for the year 2013, takes effect.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S7027A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public health law and the
administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to
prohibiting the sale of liquid nicotine to minors; and to amend the
general business law, in relation to the labeling and packaging of
electronic liquid

PURPOSE:

This bill would prohibit the sale of liquid nicotine to minors and
require liquid nicotine that is sold to be have a list of ingredients
and a warning label if the liquid contains any percentage of nicotine.
This bill also requires liquid nicotine to be sold in a child proof
container.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends Section 1399-cc of the public health law, as
amended by chapter 131 of the laws of 2011, subdivisions 2, 3, 4 and 7
as amended by chapter 448 of the laws of 2012 to include the
definition of "liquid nicotine" or "e-liquid" to mean any liquid
composed of nicotine and other chemicals, and is sold as a product
which may be used in electronic cigarettes.

Section two amends Section 17-706 of the administrative code of the
city of New York, as amended by local law number 94 of the city of New
York.

Section three amends the General Business Law by adding section 399-gg
which requires any electronic liquid for sale or offered for sale to
have a conspicuous notice stating: a) the percentage of nicotine in
such electronic liquid; and b) a list of any other ingredient in such
liquid. If the liquid contains any percentage of nicotine a warning
label must be prominently displayed which states. "WARNING: This
product contains nicotine derived from tobacco. Nicotine is an
addictive chemical." This section also requires that an electronic
liquid sold must be offered for sale in a child resistant bottle,
which is designed to prevent accidental exposure of children to
electronic liquids. Any violation of this amendment is punishable by a
civil penalty not to exceed $1,000.

Section four of this bill sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

E-cigarettes are battery powered devices that allow an individual to
inhale nicotine while emitting only vapor. The nicotine in
e-cigarettes is called "electronic liquids" or "liquid nicotine."
Liquid nicotine is a liquid composed of nicotine but is also laced
with other chemicals and substances and is often flavored. Many liquid
nicotine compounds are made on factory floors or in the back rooms of
shops and are not regulated by the federal government, however, the
FDA recently proposed e-cigarette regulations. E-liquids have been
found to be harmful to humans if ingested or simply upon contact with
an individual's skin. Between 2012 and 2013, calls to poison control
centers involving e-liquids have increased by 300 percent, with 1,351


calls in 2013. Currently, liquid nicotine is sold in sealed cartridges
or in a bottle used to refill e-cigarettes or refillable cartridges.
As of January 1, 2013, e-cigarettes are not allowed to be sold to
minors. However, current law does not ban the sale of e-liquids to
minors.

This bill would ban the sale of liquid nicotine to minors, require
child proof packaging, and require labeling requirements which include
an ingredients list and a warning label. This legislation will protect
minors by not letting them purchase liquid nicotine, and by requiring
packaging which will make children less likely to come into contact
with the liquid accidently. This legislation will also increase
awareness of the ingredients in liquid nicotine and of the dangers of
nicotine as it is an addictive chemical. This legislation will protect
individuals of all ages from the potential dangers of electronic
cigarettes, particularly given that they are unregulated and have not
been proven to be safe for use at any age.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that if
local law number 94 of the city of New York for the year 2013 shall
not have taken effect on or before such date then section two of this
act shall take effect on the same date and in the same manner as local
law number 94 of the city of New York for the year 2013, takes effect.
